# API Arena

> API Arena is a free competitive platform for students, self-taught backend developers, and teachers. You choose a challenge, build a real Spring Boot REST API, and upload the project as a ZIP. An isolated sandbox builds and runs that API, then real HTTP tests score it. It is measured practice, not a slide-only course.

Each submission is scored out of 1000. Up to 800 points come from technical HTTP tests against the running API: functional correctness (300), performance (300), and REST design (200). Up to 200 points come from an AI review. The default review rubric is heuristic, and a language-model provider can be enabled per environment. XP tracks cumulative progress. ELO is a separate competitive rating that moves against the score expected for your rating and the challenge difficulty. Submitting again below your best score on that challenge is penalized.

Create a free account and open the challenge catalog. Read the public preview, then sign in and start a timed session to see the full requirements. Zip a Maven project with pom.xml at the archive root and upload it. The pipeline builds the project in a sandbox, calls the API over HTTP, saves the score, and updates the leaderboard. The docs hub explains the first submission step by step.

A public challenge page is a preview only: title, description, difficulty, category, time limit, and XP reward. Endpoint lists, hidden tests, and hints are not on that page. They appear after you sign in and start a timed session.

API Arena is for students learning backend APIs, developers who want measured practice, and teachers who group students and review their submissions.

Website: https://apiarena.net
English: https://apiarena.net/en
Spanish: https://apiarena.net/es

## Who it is for

Students learning backend APIs, self-taught developers who want a measured score, and teachers who group students and review submissions.

## How it works

1. Pick a challenge and read the public preview.
2. Sign in and start a timed session to open the full requirements.
3. Upload a ZIP of a Maven Spring Boot project with pom.xml at the archive root.
4. An isolated sandbox builds and runs the API.
5. Real HTTP tests score functional behavior, performance, and REST design.
6. An AI review adds the remaining points. XP and ELO update. A replay is stored for debugging.

## Scoring

- Maximum score: 1000.
- Technical HTTP tests: up to 800 (functional correctness 300, performance 300, REST design 200).
- AI review: up to 200. The default rubric is heuristic. A language-model provider can be enabled per environment.
- XP is cumulative progress. ELO is a separate competitive rating. Repeating a challenge below your best score on it is penalized.

## Languages

The same public pages exist in English (/en/...) and Spanish (/es/...). Docs are translated. Challenge preview text is the catalog description.

## Docs

- [Getting Started Guide](https://apiarena.net/en/docs/guia-para-empezar): Mindset, work strategy, and delivery rhythm to progress fast without burning out.
- [First Steps](https://apiarena.net/en/docs/primeros-pasos): Practical checklist to prepare your first challenge from start to finish.
- [Preconfigure Project for Challenges](https://apiarena.net/en/docs/preconfiguracion-proyecto): Complete technical guide for prerequisites, minimum structure, and pre-submission validation.
- [Platform navigation](https://apiarena.net/en/docs/platform-navigation): Where everything lives: landing, app chrome, dashboard, challenges, submissions, Docs, and account basics.
- [Challenges catalog](https://apiarena.net/en/docs/challenges-catalog): How to search, filter, sort, and open a challenge before you start a timed run.
- [Challenge workspace](https://apiarena.net/en/docs/challenge-workspace): Challenge detail vs submit screen: what you see before and after you start a timed run.
- [Submitting a challenge](https://apiarena.net/en/docs/submitting-a-challenge): ZIP rules, pipeline expectations, and what to do while your submission is processing.
- [Common Errors](https://apiarena.net/en/docs/errores-comunes): Recurring submission failures, why they happen, and how to prevent them systematically.
- [XP and ELO System](https://apiarena.net/en/docs/sistema-xp-elo): Complete guide to classification, ELO gains/losses, and ranking strategy.

- [Guía para empezar](https://apiarena.net/es/docs/guia-para-empezar): Mentalidad, estrategia de trabajo y ritmo de entregas para progresar rápido sin quemarte.
- [Primeros pasos](https://apiarena.net/es/docs/primeros-pasos): Checklist práctica para preparar tu primer challenge de principio a fin.
- [Preconfigurar el proyecto para challenges](https://apiarena.net/es/docs/preconfiguracion-proyecto): Guía técnica completa de requisitos previos, estructura mínima y validación pre-entrega.
- [Navegación de la plataforma](https://apiarena.net/es/docs/platform-navigation): Dónde está cada cosa: landing, chrome de la app, Dashboard, Challenges, submissions, Docs y lo básico de la cuenta.
- [Catálogo de Challenges](https://apiarena.net/es/docs/challenges-catalog): Cómo buscar, filtrar, ordenar y abrir un challenge antes de iniciar una sesión cronometrada.
- [Workspace del challenge](https://apiarena.net/es/docs/challenge-workspace): Detalle del challenge vs pantalla de entrega: qué ves antes y después de iniciar una sesión cronometrada.
- [Entregar un challenge](https://apiarena.net/es/docs/submitting-a-challenge): Reglas del ZIP, expectativas del pipeline y qué hacer mientras se procesa tu entrega.
- [Errores comunes](https://apiarena.net/es/docs/errores-comunes): Fallos recurrentes en entregas, por qué ocurren y cómo prevenirlos de forma sistemática.
- [Sistema de XP y ELO](https://apiarena.net/es/docs/sistema-xp-elo): Guía completa de clasificación, ganancias/pérdidas de ELO y estrategia de ranking.

## Crawler policy

Public pages may be indexed by search engines and by GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, Applebot-Extended. Private account, teacher, and admin areas are disallowed in https://apiarena.net/robots.txt.
